# gh-912: [BUG] ls-remote branch-existence probes count git stderr warnings as branch existence — first-run branch setup dies in central mode (insteadOf)

## Description

## Goal — branch-existence probes decide on real `ls-remote` ref lines, never on stderr noise (v1)

One sentence: **a first-run branch setup in central mode (insteadOf-rewritten origin) succeeds even when every git network command prints `warning: redirecting to https://…` to stderr.**

## What actually happened (attribution — read before assuming a runtime regression)

- Reported A/B: job 56692 (dm0.1.43, 2026-10-10, green) vs job 60071 (dm0.1.48, 2026-10-16, red), same repo/sequence, branch absent both times. The dm0.1.48 pin was suspected of changing the capture contract.
- **dmtools-dart is exonerated (verified at tags v0.1.43 / v0.1.48):** the JS-bridge `cli_execute_command` (`lib/src/js/tool_bridge.dart` `_runShellScript` — wraps the command in `{ … } 2>&1`) merged stdout+stderr at BOTH tags. Capture-path files byte-identical (blob SHAs match: `cli_tools.dart` 7535dbbf, `process_output_tee.dart` 6dae9855, `property_reader.dart` b8bebff3); the only two commits in range touching `tool_bridge.dart` (#402 file_read parity, #404 console-bridge split) do not touch `_runCommandLine`/`_runShellScript`/`_executeCliTool`. The merge is deliberate Java-parity design (`redirectErrorStream(true)` note in-source); no flag gates it.
- **agents/js is unchanged in the 2026-10-08..16 window:** zero commits on `checkoutBranch.js`; `preCliDevelopmentSetup.js` got one unrelated hunk (f013a26, tracker migration); `gitOps.js`/`pullRequest.js` capture paths byte-identical pre/post window; no tool-surface switch ever existed. `cleanCommandOutput` has carried the same 4-filter, warning-blind body since ≥ 2026-05-31 (e5ce66b era).
- **Env-delta closure (verified; supersedes the earlier [INFERENCE]):** the runner is IDENTICAL across the A/B pair (runner 4f4080802afd, gitlab-runner 19.0.1, same slot), and the insteadOf bootstrap line is byte-identical in both traces (trace :59: `git config --global url."https://oauth2:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@git.customsmobile.com/".insteadOf "https://git.customsmobile.com/"`). `grep -c redirecting` = 0 in job 56692 (dm0.1.43 image) vs present on EVERY network command in job 60071 (dm0.1.48 image). The warning is **version-gated git behavior, not an insteadOf artifact**: `git ls-remote` against a GitLab URL that the server redirects prints `warning: redirecting to <url>/` on git **2.54.0** (reproduced locally, with and without insteadOf-injected credentials), while git **2.43.0** follows the same redirect silently (repro against the same live server, empty stderr). Base-image tags are static in the window (1.0.0/1.0.1 2026-09-17, 1.1.0 2026-09-18); the two prebuilt tags were BUILT on different dates (dm0.1.43 ~2026-10-07, dm0.1.48 ~2026-10-14) with independently refreshed apt layers — the git binary bump inside the newer image is the prime suspect. Image-internal `git version` check (`fa1.0.522-dm0.1.43-node24` vs `fa1.0.522-dm0.1.48-node24`) is pending owner-side (no container runtime on the research host); a server-side GitLab change in the window is not 100% excluded but the 2.43-silent vs 2.54-warn repro against the same server argues for the git version. **Net: worked-then-broke = image content delta (git binary), NOT dmtools version, NOT agents/js, NOT runner config. The latent warning-blind-probe defect is older than both images (≥ 2026-05-31) and fires only when BOTH hold: the branch is genuinely absent (per-ticket first run — after one success the real ref line rides along and `.trim()` works by accident) AND the newer git prints the redirect warning.**

## Root cause (this repo, verified)

`cleanCommandOutput` (canonical `js/common/pullRequest.js:8-16` + 17 byte-identical inline copies + 4 delegates) filters only script-wrapper artifacts (`Script started` / `Script done` / `COMMAND=` / `COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=`). Git stderr (`warning: redirecting to …`) survives cleaning, and the JS bridge hands probes stdout+stderr merged. Every branch-existence probe that branches on capture `.trim()` emptiness then reads a warning-only capture as "branch exists on remote".

Failure chain (reported case): `preCliDevelopmentSetup.js:259-260` probe → capture = `'warning: redirecting to …'` → deciding line `:265 if (remoteBranches.trim())` → `:270` fetch of the missing ref fails (caught) → `:275 git checkout -B <b> origin/<b>` → `fatal: 'origin/<b>' is not a commit` → `action()` rethrows `:563-568`, `:631-634` → **preCliJSAction dies before the CLI agent starts**.

## Blast radius — 14 vulnerable sites (8 beyond the original report)

| Class | Sites | Effect of warning-only capture |
|---|---|---|
| **FATAL** | `preCliDevelopmentSetup.js:259-265, :289-291` (dev+feature probes); `js/common/gitOps.js:65-66` (`_switchToBranch`, fatal for preCliReworkSetup `:426-428`) | "exists" → fetch+`checkout -B origin/<b>` → fatal → dev job dies pre-agent |
| Non-fatal wrong-branch | `checkoutBranch.js:76-78, :129-135`; `preCliTestAutomationSetup.js:157-161`; `preCliMobileTestAutomationSetup.js:110-114`; `preCliStoryTestAutomationSetup.js:92-94`; `developTicketAndCreatePR.js:76-83` (suffix `_1` branch name) | agent proceeds on wrong/base branch |
| Inverse masking (absent looks present) | `postMobileTestAutomationResults.js:280-284` (skips `push -u --force`); `postStoryTestAutomationResults.js:346-352, :383-388`; `postTestAutomationResults.js:208-214, :245-250`; `pushReworkChanges.js:372-375`; `storyTestAutomationRework.js:161-162`; `postTestReworkResults.js:294-297` | push skipped or failed push masked as "branch not found" |
| **Worst:** SHA poisoning | `postTestReworkResults.js:299-302` — `remoteSha = capture.split(/\s+/)[0]` | stderr-first merge order → `remoteSha = 'warning:'` → false "Push rejected" even on success |
| Immune (6 sites) | `indexOf('refs/heads/<b>')` form: `developTicketAndCreatePR.js:183,370,405,862`; `preCliTestReworkSetup.js:77-78`; `prepareTestPRForReview.js:205-206`; all local-git emptiness consumers (`branch --list`, `status`, `rev-parse`, …) | none — warning lines lack `refs/heads/` |

## Proposed fix — defense in the probe

**(a) Strict ref-line parsing (primary):** add to `js/common/pullRequest.js` (next to `ensureRemoteBranchRef :275-288`):

```js
// A branch exists on origin iff the ls-remote capture contains a real ref line.
// Tolerates stderr noise (insteadOf warnings) merged into the capture.
function remoteBranchExists(runCommand, workingDir, branchName) {
    var out = cleanCommandOutput(runCommand(workingDir,
        'git ls-remote --heads origin ' + quoteBranch(branchName)));
    var re = new RegExp('^[0-9a-f]{7,40}\\trefs/heads/' + escapeRe(branchName) + '$', 'm');
    return re.test(out);
}
```

Migrate the 14 vulnerable sites (13 files) onto it. `postTestReworkResults.js:294-302` additionally parses the SHA from the matched ref line — never `split(/\s+/)[0]` of line 1.

**(b) Warning filter in `cleanCommandOutput` (secondary, defense in depth):** drop lines matching line-start `/^warning: /` and `/^note: /` (anchored — never mid-line, diffs/logs may contain the words). Consolidate the 17 inline copies onto the `prHelper` canonical (per repo rule gh-823) so the filter exists once.

Tiering: **core** = (a) at the 3 FATAL sites + `remoteBranchExists` helper; **second tier** = (a) at the remaining 11 sites and (b); **excluded** = asking dmtools-dart to un-merge streams (deliberate Java-parity contract; separate coordination if ever wanted).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — `preCliDevelopmentSetup.checkoutBranch` with a warning-only ls-remote capture (stdout empty) takes the create-branch path and the action completes (currently: fatal).
- **AC2** — same for `gitOps._switchToBranch` (preCliReworkSetup path no longer calls `failSetup`).
- **AC3** — a real ref line `<40-hex>\trefs/heads/<b>` in a warning-polluted capture still classifies "exists" (both orders: warning before/after the ref line).
- **AC4** — `postTestReworkResults` push-verify extracts the SHA from the ref line; warning-only capture no longer yields `remoteSh…

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

blocks.text:
# gh-912: [BUG] ls-remote branch-existence probes count git stderr warnings as branch existence — first-run branch setup dies in central mode (insteadOf)

## Description

## Goal — branch-existence probes decide on real `ls-remote` ref lines, never on stderr noise (v1)

One sentence: **a first-run branch setup in central mode (insteadOf-rewritten origin) succeeds even when every git network command prints `warning: redirecting to https://…` to stderr.**

## What actually happened (attribution — read before assuming a runtime regression)

- Reported A/B: job 56692 (dm0.1.43, 2026-10-10, green) vs job 60071 (dm0.1.48, 2026-10-16, red), same repo/sequence, branch absent both times. The dm0.1.48 pin was suspected of changing the capture contract.
- **dmtools-dart is exonerated (verified at tags v0.1.43 / v0.1.48):** the JS-bridge `cli_execute_command` (`lib/src/js/tool_bridge.dart` `_runShellScript` — wraps the command in `{ … } 2>&1`) merged stdout+stderr at BOTH tags. Capture-path files byte-identical (blob SHAs match: `cli_tools.dart` 7535dbbf, `process_output_tee.dart` 6dae9855, `property_reader.dart` b8bebff3); the only two commits in range touching `tool_bridge.dart` (#402 file_read parity, #404 console-bridge split) do not touch `_runCommandLine`/`_runShellScript`/`_executeCliTool`. The merge is deliberate Java-parity design (`redirectErrorStream(true)` note in-source); no flag gates it.
- **agents/js is unchanged in the 2026-10-08..16 window:** zero commits on `checkoutBranch.js`; `preCliDevelopmentSetup.js` got one unrelated hunk (f013a26, tracker migration); `gitOps.js`/`pullRequest.js` capture paths byte-identical pre/post window; no tool-surface switch ever existed. `cleanCommandOutput` has carried the same 4-filter, warning-blind body since ≥ 2026-05-31 (e5ce66b era).
- **Env-delta closure (verified; supersedes the earlier [INFERENCE]):** the runner is IDENTICAL across the A/B pair (runner 4f4080802afd, gitlab-runner 19.0.1, same slot), and the insteadOf bootstrap line is byte-identical in both traces (trace :59: `git config --global url."https://oauth2:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@git.customsmobile.com/".insteadOf "https://git.customsmobile.com/"`). `grep -c redirecting` = 0 in job 56692 (dm0.1.43 image) vs present on EVERY network command in job 60071 (dm0.1.48 image). The warning is **version-gated git behavior, not an insteadOf artifact**: `git ls-remote` against a GitLab URL that the server redirects prints `warning: redirecting to <url>/` on git **2.54.0** (reproduced locally, with and without insteadOf-injected credentials), while git **2.43.0** follows the same redirect silently (repro against the same live server, empty stderr). Base-image tags are static in the window (1.0.0/1.0.1 2026-09-17, 1.1.0 2026-09-18); the two prebuilt tags were BUILT on different dates (dm0.1.43 ~2026-10-07, dm0.1.48 ~2026-10-14) with independently refreshed apt layers — the git binary bump inside the newer image is the prime suspect. Image-internal `git version` check (`fa1.0.522-dm0.1.43-node24` vs `fa1.0.522-dm0.1.48-node24`) is pending owner-side (no container runtime on the research host); a server-side GitLab change in the window is not 100% excluded but the 2.43-silent vs 2.54-warn repro against the same server argues for the git version. **Net: worked-then-broke = image content delta (git binary), NOT dmtools version, NOT agents/js, NOT runner config. The latent warning-blind-probe defect is older than both images (≥ 2026-05-31) and fires only when BOTH hold: the branch is genuinely absent (per-ticket first run — after one success the real ref line rides along and `.trim()` works by accident) AND the newer git prints the redirect warning.**

## Root cause (this repo, verified)

`cleanCommandOutput` (canonical `js/common/pullRequest.js:8-16` + 17 byte-identical inline copies + 4 delegates) filters only script-wrapper artifacts (`Script started` / `Script done` / `COMMAND=` / `COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=`). Git stderr (`warning: redirecting to …`) survives cleaning, and the JS bridge hands probes stdout+stderr merged. Every branch-existence probe that branches on capture `.trim()` emptiness then reads a warning-only capture as "branch exists on remote".

Failure chain (reported case): `preCliDevelopmentSetup.js:259-260` probe → capture = `'warning: redirecting to …'` → deciding line `:265 if (remoteBranches.trim())` → `:270` fetch of the missing ref fails (caught) → `:275 git checkout -B <b> origin/<b>` → `fatal: 'origin/<b>' is not a commit` → `action()` rethrows `:563-568`, `:631-634` → **preCliJSAction dies before the CLI agent starts**.

## Blast radius — 14 vulnerable sites (8 beyond the original report)

| Class | Sites | Effect of warning-only capture |
|---|---|---|
| **FATAL** | `preCliDevelopmentSetup.js:259-265, :289-291` (dev+feature probes); `js/common/gitOps.js:65-66` (`_switchToBranch`, fatal for preCliReworkSetup `:426-428`) | "exists" → fetch+`checkout -B origin/<b>` → fatal → dev job dies pre-agent |
| Non-fatal wrong-branch | `checkoutBranch.js:76-78, :129-135`; `preCliTestAutomationSetup.js:157-161`; `preCliMobileTestAutomationSetup.js:110-114`; `preCliStoryTestAutomationSetup.js:92-94`; `developTicketAndCreatePR.js:76-83` (suffix `_1` branch name) | agent proceeds on wrong/base branch |
| Inverse masking (absent looks present) | `postMobileTestAutomationResults.js:280-284` (skips `push -u --force`); `postStoryTestAutomationResults.js:346-352, :383-388`; `postTestAutomationResults.js:208-214, :245-250`; `pushReworkChanges.js:372-375`; `storyTestAutomationRework.js:161-162`; `postTestReworkResults.js:294-297` | push skipped or failed push masked as "branch not found" |
| **Worst:** SHA poisoning | `postTestReworkResults.js:299-302` — `remoteSha = capture.split(/\s+/)[0]` | stderr-first merge order → `remoteSha = 'warning:'` → false "Push rejected" even on success |
| Immune (6 sites) | `indexOf('refs/heads/<b>')` form: `developTicketAndCreatePR.js:183,370,405,862`; `preCliTestReworkSetup.js:77-78`; `prepareTestPRForReview.js:205-206`; all local-git emptiness consumers (`branch --list`, `status`, `rev-parse`, …) | none — warning lines lack `refs/heads/` |

## Proposed fix — defense in the probe

**(a) Strict ref-line parsing (primary):** add to `js/common/pullRequest.js` (next to `ensureRemoteBranchRef :275-288`):

```js
// A branch exists on origin iff the ls-remote capture contains a real ref line.
// Tolerates stderr noise (insteadOf warnings) merged into the capture.
function remoteBranchExists(runCommand, workingDir, branchName) {
    var out = cleanCommandOutput(runCommand(workingDir,
        'git ls-remote --heads origin ' + quoteBranch(branchName)));
    var re = new RegExp('^[0-9a-f]{7,40}\\trefs/heads/' + escapeRe(branchName) + '$', 'm');
    return re.test(out);
}
```

Migrate the 14 vulnerable sites (13 files) onto it. `postTestReworkResults.js:294-302` additionally parses the SHA from the matched ref line — never `split(/\s+/)[0]` of line 1.

**(b) Warning filter in `cleanCommandOutput` (secondary, defense in depth):** drop lines matching line-start `/^warning: /` and `/^note: /` (anchored — never mid-line, diffs/logs may contain the words). Consolidate the 17 inline copies onto the `prHelper` canonical (per repo rule gh-823) so the filter exists once.

Tiering: **core** = (a) at the 3 FATAL sites + `remoteBranchExists` helper; **second tier** = (a) at the remaining 11 sites and (b); **excluded** = asking dmtools-dart to un-merge streams (deliberate Java-parity contract; separate coordination if ever wanted).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — `preCliDevelopmentSetup.checkoutBranch` with a warning-only ls-remote capture (stdout empty) takes the create-branch path and the action completes (currently: fatal).
- **AC2** — same for `gitOps._switchToBranch` (preCliReworkSetup path no longer calls `failSetup`).
- **AC3** — a real ref line `<40-hex>\trefs/heads/<b>` in a warning-polluted capture still classifies "exists" (both orders: warning before/after the ref line).
- **AC4** — `postTestReworkResults` push-verify extracts the SHA from the ref line; warning-only capture no longer yields `remoteSh…

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

- One subtle issue: the regex `^([0-9a-f]{7,40})\trefs/heads/<escaped>\r?$` with 'm' flag. With the `m` flag, `$` matches before `\n` but ALSO... wait `\r?$` — if line ends with `\r`, then `\r?` consumes it and `$` matches at the `\n` boundary. OK.
- What about a branch name that is a prefix of another branch name? E.g. branchName = `feature/x`, and remote has `feature/xyz`. The regex: `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}\trefs/heads/feature/x\r?$` — `feature/xyz` line would be `...refs/heads/feature/xyz`, the regex requires `feature/x` followed by `\r?$`. `\r?` doesn't match `y`, `$` doesn't match mid-line (with m flag, `$` matches before `\n`). So `feature/xyz` does NOT satisfy the regex for `feature/x`. Good — the `$` anchor prevents prefix collisions.
- BUT WAIT: ls-remote with a specific branch pattern: `git ls-remote --heads origin <branch>` — does ls-remote do exact matching or pattern matching? `git ls-remote` treats the pattern as a glob pattern matched against refs. If branchName contains glob special chars like `*`, they'd be treated as wildcards by git. E.g. branch `feature/*` — but that's not a valid branch name anyway. Branch names can't contain `*`. But they can contain `[`, `?`, `!`... Actually git branch names can contain `[` and `?`? Ref naming rules: no space, no `~ ^ : ? * [ \`. So `?`, `*`, `[` are invalid in branch names. blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

Now I understand the core helper. Let me examine the migrated sites in detail. Key areas to review:

1. `remoteBranchSha` — the regex: `'^([0-9a-f]{7,40})\\trefs/heads/' + escapeRegExp(branchName) + '\\r?$'` with 'm' flag.

Potential issues:
- `escapeRegExp(branchName)` — escaped correctly.
- BUT: the branch name is not quoted in the command `git ls-remote --heads origin ' + branchName`. This was pre-existing (probe command built without quoting), but now `checkoutBranch.js` uses `runCommandForProbes` and `remoteBranchExists`. Let me check whether the pre-existing code quoted the branch name. In the old code: `'git ls-remote --heads origin ' + branchName` — same, unquoted. So pre-existing behavior, not a regression. However, since the regex uses escapeRegExp, and the command is unquoted — a branch name with spaces would break the command. Pre-existing.
- One subtle issue: the regex `^([0-9a-f]{7,40})\trefs/heads/<escaped>\r?$` with 'm' flag. With the `m` flag, `$` matches before `\n` but ALSO... wait `\r?$` — if line ends with `\r`, then `\r?` consumes it and `$` matches at the `\n` boundary. OK.
- What about a branch name that is a prefix of another branch name? E.g. branchName = `feature/x`, and remote has `feature/xyz`. The regex: `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}\trefs/heads/feature/x\r?$` — `feature/xyz` line would be `...refs/heads/feature/xyz`, the regex requires `feature/x` followed by `\r?$`. `\r?` doesn't match `y`, `$` doesn't match mid-line (with m flag, `$` matches before `\n`). So `feature/xyz` does NOT satisfy the regex for `feature/x`. Good — the `$` anchor prevents prefix collisions.
- BUT WAIT: ls-remote with a specific branch pattern: `git ls-remote --heads origin <branch>` — does ls-remote do exact matching or pattern matching? `git ls-remote` treats the pattern as a glob pattern matched against refs. Now I understand the core helper. Let me examine the migrated sites in detail. Key areas to review:

1. `remoteBranchSha` — the regex: `'^([0-9a-f]{7,40})\\trefs/heads/' + escapeRegExp(branchName) + '\\r?$'` with 'm' flag.

Potential issues:
- `escapeRegExp(branchName)` — escaped correctly.
- BUT: the branch name is not quoted in the command `git ls-remote --heads origin ' + branchName`. This was pre-existing (probe command built without quoting), but now `checkoutBranch.js` uses `runCommandForProbes` and `remoteBranchExists`. Let me check whether the pre-existing code quoted the branch name. In the old code: `'git ls-remote --heads origin ' + branchName` — same, unquoted. So pre-existing behavior, not a regression. However, since the regex uses escapeRegExp, and the command is unquoted — a branch name with spaces would break the command. Pre-existing.
- One subtle issue: the regex `^([0-9a-f]{7,40})\trefs/heads/<escaped>\r?$` with 'm' flag. With the `m` flag, `$` matches before `\n` but ALSO... wait `\r?$` — if line ends with `\r`, then `\r?` consumes it and `$` matches at the `\n` boundary. OK.
- What about a branch name that is a prefix of another branch name? E.g. branchName = `feature/x`, and remote has `feature/xyz`. The regex: `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}\trefs/heads/feature/x\r?$` — `feature/xyz` line would be `...refs/heads/feature/xyz`, the regex requires `feature/x` followed by `\r?$`. `\r?` doesn't match `y`, `$` doesn't match mid-line (with m flag, `$` matches before `\n`). So `feature/xyz` does NOT satisfy the regex for `feature/x`. Good — the `$` anchor prevents prefix collisions.
- BUT WAIT: ls-remote with a specific branch pattern: `git ls-remote --heads origin <branch>` — does ls-remote do exact matching or pattern matching? `git ls-remote` treats the pattern as a glob pattern matched against refs. If branchName contains glob special chars like `*`, they'd be treated as wildcards by git. E.g. branch `feature/*` — but that's not a valid branch name anyway. Branch names can't contain `*`. But they can contain `[`, `?`, `!`... Actually git branch names can contain `[` and `?`? Ref naming rules: no space, no `~ ^ : ? * [ \`. So `?`, `*`, `[` are invalid in branch names. So glob patterns can't cause false positives via branch names. And `escapeRegExp` handles regex-special chars for the JS side. OK.

- `\r?$` handling: The capture was cleaned through `cleanCommandOutput` which trims, so trailing `\r` may persist if lines end with `\r\n`. Handled.

2. `remoteRefLines` — filter `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}\trefs\//`. Not anchored to end, intentionally loose (keeps all ref lines: heads and tags). Exported but is it used anywhere? Let me check usage. It's exported. Used by tests maybe, or by postTestReworkResults? Let me check.

3. The `quoteBranch` mentioned in the ticket's proposed fix — the ticket suggested `quoteBranch(branchName)` in the command, but the implementation doesn't quote. The old code didn't quote either. Not a regression but worth noting the probe command is unchanged. Actually wait — the proposed fix in the ticket had `'git ls-remote --heads origin ' + quoteBranch(branchName)`. The implementation: `'git ls-remote --heads origin ' + branchName`. Is there a quoteBranch helper in pullRequest.js? Let me check. If not — the ticket's proposed fix included quoting for shell safety; the implementation skipped it. That's a deviation from the ticket spec (minor, since pre-existing). But since branch names from tickets (e.g. `feature/AITS-123`) are typically safe... but branch names could contain characters that break shell quoting — e.g. `develop_ticket(x)`. Pre-existing though.

4. Behavior change in `remoteBranchSha`: throws through when probe fails. Callers: some wrapped in try/catch. Let me check each migrated site for error-path consistency. Previously `cleanCommandOutput(cmd(...) || '')` — if cmd throws, the exception propagates (callers wrapped in try/catch in some sites). Now `remoteBranchExists` throws the same way. Consistent.

5. Important behavioral check — in `gitOps._switchToBranch`, old code called `cleanCommandOutput(cmd(...))` and decided on `.trim()`. New code calls `prHelper.remoteBranchExists(cmd, null, branchName)`. Wait — `workingDir` param: `cmd` in gitOps takes `(command)` only? Let me check `_switchToBranch(branchName, cmd)` — the cmd signature. `remoteBranchExists(runCommand, workingDir, branchName)` calls `runCommand('git ls-remote --heads origin ' + branchName, workingDir)`. If gitOps' `cmd` only accepts `command`, passing workingDir as second arg is harmless (ignored). OK.

6. In `checkoutBranch.js`, the new `runCommandForProbes(command)` adapter — signature `(command)` only, ignores workingDir — passes `{ command: command }` without workingDirectory. The action always runs in job root per comment. OK.

Wait — there's a subtle bug potential in checkoutBranch.js: `var remoteBranchExists = false;` declared as a local variable named same as helper... `prHelper.remoteBranchExists(...)` is called and assigned to local `remoteBranchExists`. That's fine in JS — no shadowing issue since it's `prHelper.remoteBranchExists`.

7. The regex `'\\t'` — requires TAB separator. ls-remote output uses TAB. Real. Mocks updated. But what if the JS bridge normalizes tabs? Unlikely.

8. `{7,40}` — full SHAs are 40 hex; shortened from ls-remote? ls-remote always prints full 40-hex SHAs. `{7,40}` fine.

9. Potential issue: `remoteBranchSha` builds regex from `branchName` — branch names could be long; regex length fine.

10. `cleanCommandOutput` now filters `^warning: ` and `^note: ` lines. This affects ALL existing call sites of cleanCommandOutput across the repo — including places that parse `git diff`, logs, etc. E.g., `readStagedDiffStat`, `extractPrUrl`... Could filtering `^warning: `/`^note: ` lines break any legit consumer? A git diff line starting with "warning: "? Diffs have `+`/`-` prefixes, so no. `git status` — no. gh CLI output — a `warning:` line from gh could be dropped; that's the intent.     "summary": "[BUG] ls-remote branch-existence probes count git stderr warnings as branch existence — first-run branch setup dies in central mode (insteadOf)",
    "description": "## Goal — branch-existence probes decide on real `ls-remote` ref lines, never on stderr noise (v1)

One sentence: **a first-run branch setup in central mode (insteadOf-rewritten origin) succeeds even when every git network command prints `warning: redirecting to https://…` to stderr.**

## What actually happened (attribution — read before assuming a runtime regression)

- Reported A/B: job 56692 (dm0.1.43, 2026-10-10, green) vs job 60071 (dm0.1.48, 2026-10-16, red), same repo/sequence, branch absent both times. The dm0.1.48 pin was suspected of changing the capture contract.

Capture-path files byte-identical (blob SHAs match: `cli_tools.dart` 7535dbbf, `process_output_tee.dart` 6dae9855, `property_reader.dart` b8bebff3); the only two commits in range touching `tool_bridge.dart` (#402 file_read parity, #404 console-bridge split) do not touch `_runCommandLine`/`_runShellScript`/`_executeCliTool`. The warning is **version-gated git behavior, not an insteadOf artifact**: `git ls-remote` against a GitLab URL that the server redirects prints `warning: redirecting to <url>/` on git **2.54.0** (reproduced locally, with and without insteadOf-injected credentials), while git **2.43.0** follows the same redirect silently (repro against the same live server, empty stderr). Base-image tags are static in the window (1.0.0/1.0.1 2026-09-17, 1.1.0 2026-09-18); the two prebuilt tags were BUILT on different dates (dm0.1.43 ~2026-10-07, dm0.1.48 ~2026-10-14) with independently refreshed apt layers — the git binary bump inside the newer image is the prime suspect. ## Root cause (this repo, verified)

`cleanCommandOutput` (canonical `js/common/pullRequest.js:8-16` + 17 byte-identical inline copies + 4 delegates) filters only script-wrapper artifacts (`Script started` / `Script done` / `COMMAND=` / `COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=`). Git stderr (`warning: redirecting to …`) survives cleaning, and the JS bridge hands probes stdout+stderr merged. Every branch-existence probe that branches on capture `.trim()` emptiness then reads a warning-only capture as "branch exists on remote".

## Proposed fix — defense in the probe

**(a) Strict ref-line parsing (primary):** add to `js/common/pullRequest.js` (next to `ensureRemoteBranchRef :275-288`):

```js
// A branch exists on origin iff the ls-remote capture contains a real ref line.
// Tolerates stderr noise (insteadOf warnings) merged into the capture.
function remoteBranchExists(runCommand, workingDir, branchName) {
    var out = cleanCommandOutput(runCommand(workingDir,
        'git ls-remote --heads origin ' + quoteBranch(branchName)));
    var re = new RegExp('^[0-9a-f]{7,40}\\trefs/heads/' + escapeRe(branchName) + '$', 'm');
    return re.test(out);
}
```

Migrate the 14 vulnerable sites (13 files) onto it. `postTestReworkResults.js:294-302` additionally parses the SHA from the matched ref line — never `split(/\s+/)[0]` of line 1.

**(b) Warning filter in `cleanCommandOutput` (secondary, defense in depth):** drop lines matching line-start `/^warning: /` and `/^note: /` (anchored — never mid-line, diffs/logs may contain the words). Consolidate the 17 inline copies onto the `prHelper` canonical (per repo rule gh-823) so the filter exists once.

💡 **SUGGESTION: canonical probe interpolates the branch name into the shell command unquoted**

`remoteBranchSha` (and therefore `remoteBranchExists`) builds the probe as:

```js
var out = cleanCommandOutput(runCommand('git ls-remote --heads origin ' + branchName, workingDir) || '');
```

The ticket's proposed fix (section "Proposed fix (a)") explicitly wrapped the name: `'git ls-remote --heads origin ' + quoteBranch(branchName)` — that quoting was dropped in the implementation. The name is now regex-escaped (good, E2) but not shell-escaped, and this helper is the **single probe for 13 files**, so this is the right place to harden it.

Risk assessment (why this is only a suggestion): dmtools' CliCommandExecutor rejects `;`, `|`, `>`, `<`, backticks, `$(...)` etc., so command injection is not reachable; but a config-derived branch name containing a space or `"` (custom `branchName` templates in `.dmtools/config.js`) would silently probe a different refspec, classify "absent", and push the first run down the create-branch path. The repo already quotes exactly this way elsewhere (`git branch --list "' + featureBranchName + '"'` in `checkoutBranch.js`), so the fix is consistent with existing patterns:

```js
var out = cleanCommandOutput(runCommand('git ls-remote --heads origin "' + branchName + '"', workingDir) || '');
```

Non-blocking — current callers (ticket-key/config-derived names) are safe in practice.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `escapeRegExp` is now the third identical copy in the repo**

This PR adds `escapeRegExp` to `pullRequest.js`; byte-equivalent helpers already exist at `js/common/contentOutput.js:260` and `js/mergeTrigger.js:78`:

```js
return String(text).replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
```

Understandable choice for this PR — requiring `contentOutput.js` (a heavy output-routing module) or `mergeTrigger.js` from `pullRequest.js` just for one line would add real dependency weight, and consolidating all copies was explicitly not required by the ticket. For a future cleanup: a tiny `js/common/regexUtils.js` (or re-export through an existing low-dep common module) would leave exactly one implementation. No action required for this merge.
